plainLanguage: Two months of pec deck training made the chest muscle thicker than doing nothing.
qualifiers: One trial. Group allocation is described but randomisation sequence, allocation concealment and blinded outcome assessment are not reported.
Muscle thickness was measured at a single supra-axillary site, so the result says nothing about regional growth.

In the same trial, fifteen minutes a day of pectoral static stretching produced a statistically indistinguishable thickness change, which constrains how confidently this result can be attributed to the resistance training specifically.
The machine butterfly is a related condition, not the index bilateral standing cable fly at shoulder height.

conditions: machine butterfly, 5 x 10-12 at 10-12RM, 90 s rest, three times weekly for 8 weeks, against a non-training control
scope.population: recreationally active adults, physically active at least twice weekly, without chest or shoulder injury or surgery in the previous six months

sourceLinks.locator: Methods, intervention; Results, Muscle thickness (strength group versus control, right d = 0.533 p = 0.029, left d = 0.721 p = 0.002; intervention groups indistinguishable, right p = 0.983, left p = 0.905)
Abstract (operator experience is a measurable error source in ultrasound measurement of this muscle)

statement: Eight weeks of machine butterfly training, five sets of 10 to 12 repetitions at a 10-12RM load three times weekly, increased pectoralis major muscle thickness compared with a non-training control in recreationally active adults.
